message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a three‑day stretch that includes a statutory holiday and at least one weekend day.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if needed) | Long‑weekend span |
|---------|-------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sun) | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Jan 1–3** |
| Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, NB, PE) | Feb 20 (Mon) | – | **Feb 18–20** |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Fri) | – | **Apr 7–9** |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Mon) | – | **May 20–22** |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Sat) | Observed Mon Jul 3 | **Jun 30–Jul 3** |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Mon) | – | **Sep 2–4** |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Mon) | – | **Oct 7–9** |
| Christmas | Dec 25 (Mon) | – | **Dec 23–25** |

> **Notes**  
> * The dates above are the statutory holiday dates for the federal government and most provinces. Some provinces (e.g., Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Newfoundland & Labrador) have different holidays or observe them on different days, so the long‑weekend spans may vary slightly for residents there.  
> * For holidays that fall on a weekend, the “observed” date is the following Monday (unless the holiday itself is a weekend day, in which case the holiday is simply celebrated on that day).  

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app! If you need province‑specific details or want to confirm the exact dates for a particular province, let me know and I can help you locate the official provincial holiday calendars.
